intended_object: The facet of an n-simplex opposite vertex i: the (n−1)-simplex spanned by all vertices except the i-th one. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The definition takes `s.face` on the vertex set `{i}ᶜ`, which has n elements, giving an (n−1)-simplex made of all vertices except vertex i. That is exactly the face opposite vertex i. `[NeZero n]` correctly excludes n = 0, where a single point has no non-empty proper face, and with n ≥ 1 the subtraction `n - 1` is the true value. The setting (a ring k, an affine space over a module) is the same generality Mathlib uses for `Affine.Simplex`, so the definition is not too narrow.
